## Description

Superseded scope (ADR-016): the reviewer queue lists organisation onboarding requests (type Clinic or Hospital, country, submitted date, documents, state), not doctors. The reviewer opens the uploaded documents, then approves, asks for changes with a plain reason, rejects with a reason, or later suspends an approved organisation. The queue reads only the control-plane request and documents through its own narrow, reviewed read path (ADR-014), never patient data. Extends the simple queue and documented API built in MDV-P1-064 (documents view, suspension, reviewer roles).  The design (10 Nov 2026) now shows this screen: queue filters Waiting, Needs changes, Decided, All; detail with profile, documents with checks, decision, reason, email preview and history.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given an organisation is Submitted, when a reviewer approves it, then reviewer, documents checked and time are recorded and the organisation can register patients.
- [ ] **AC2.** Given a reviewer asks for changes or rejects, when it is saved, then the applicant gets the reason in plain words by email and on the status page.
- [ ] **AC3.** Given an organisation is suspended, when staff sign in, then new registration, booking and signing are refused and existing records stay readable for care.
- [ ] **AC4.** Given a Hospital request without a signed DPA, when a reviewer tries to approve, then the server refuses and offers Ask for changes (design 10 Nov 2026).
- [ ] **AC5.** Given a Suspended organisation, when operations or a reviewer reinstates it with a reason, then it is Approved again and the owner is emailed.
- [ ] **AC6.** Given a support or finance user, when they open a request, then they can read it but approve, ask for changes, reject and suspend are refused with 403.
- [ ] **AC7.** Given a document, when a reviewer opens it, then it shows in a watermarked viewer with no download and the view is logged.
- [ ] **AC8.** Given any queue endpoint, when it returns data, then it holds no patient field (architecture test); every action needs a reason.
